source.publisher: Mid-Ulster Mail (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: returned unopposed: no contests (Belfast News-Letter, 18 May 1955, p. 8); 'Messrs. Francis Cush and Patrick M'Grath, on behalf of the Nationalists' spoke at the new council's first meeting, where M'Ilgorm, Nimmons and Morrow were the co-opted members (Mid-Ulster Mail, 18 June 1955, p. 2, image read); at the end of the term 'Mr. Francis Cush, who has been Nationalist member for Clonavaddy for 30 years, is not seeking re-election' (Northern Whig, 21 May 1958, p. 9, image read)

note: Triennial election of the 19 electoral divisions of Dungannon rural district, one member each. Nominations closed on 17 May 1955 and there were no contests: '13 Unionists and six Nationalists were returned unopposed' (Belfast News-Letter, 18 May 1955, p. 8). No poll was held; Tyrone's polling day was Thursday 2 June 1955. At the new council's first meeting Mr. M. Busby was re-elected chairman and Hugh M'Ilgorm, John Nimmons and Samuel Morrow were co-opted (Mid-Ulster Mail, 18 June 1955, p. 2). Council-meeting method: division inferred from the 2 June 1949 return (Clonavaddy: F. Cush, Northern Whig, 18 May 1949, p. 4); the Mid-Ulster Mail, 18 June 1955, p. 2 names him speaking for the Nationalists at the first meeting of the new council, and the Northern Whig, 21 May 1958, p. 9 names him as the retiring member for Clonavaddy at the next election. Returned unopposed.
